stories.title: Less drama, more listening, but is Kozo Tashima the candidate to topple Infantino?
summary: Japan FA honorary president is hoping a calmer approach that makes fewer unwelcome headlines for Fifa will be welcomed by footballNot many remember Japan’s bid for the 2022 World Cup, when the country finished the race with only two of the final 22 votes.

Kozo Tashima was involved then, and now the honorary president of the Japan Football Association is going it alone in the hope of ousting Gianni Infantino.The 68-year-old Tashima is an unlikely insurgent and an unlikely challenger to Infantino.
He is, however, a familiar and respected figure in Asian and global football politics, and ready to take the Fifa presidency out of the headlines into a quieter era.

stories.title: ‘All-out war’: UK sports fear an uncertain future after new body created
summary: Creation of Sport Org sparks disquiet at governing bodiesSmaller sports concerned they might be taken overThe leaders of Britain’s Olympic and Paralympic sports have been responsible for some of the country’s greatest successes over the past two decades.
But there are changes afoot that are increasingly ruffling feathers and stoking fears.Most people will not have heard of Sport Org, the organisation recently set up by UK Sport.
Essentially, it evolved out of British Curling, and now uses its leaders and expertise across curling, para-curling, para table tennis, squash and, from 2030, bobsleigh and skeleton.

stories.title: Meeting of two lost souls: can Pochettino make it work at Manchester United? | Barney Ronay
summary: There is nothing surprising in the news Manchester United may be on the verge of appointing Mauricio Pochettino.
United are always on the verge of appointing Pochettino.

This is a club that has spent 13 years hiring and firing the same structurally doomed manager – same shellshocked eyes, same irresolvable macro-problems – and the last eight years almost but not quite doing this to Pochettino.Well, maybe we’re finally here.

stories.title: Jockey Tom O’Brien, Cheltenham festival winner, dies aged 39
summary: O’Brien rode more than 1,000 winners over jumps‘Tom meant so much to so many people across our sport’Tom O’Brien, who rode more than 1,000 winners over jumps including five Grade Ones and two at the Cheltenham festival, has died at the age of 39 after being diagnosed with cancer.O’Brien, who retired from race riding in April 2023, had a close association with Philip Hobbs’s stable near Minehead throughout his 20-year career in the saddle and enjoyed his most prestigious Grade One victories aboard Hobbs’s Thyme Hill in the Stayers’ Hurdle at Aintree in April 2021 and the Kauto Star Novice Chase at Kempton in December 2022.

stories.title: Manchester United reach framework deal with Pochettino before settling Carrick’s fate
summary: Pochettino wants to leave USA role for UnitedUnited board meeting scheduled for WednesdayManchester United have a framework agreement with Mauricio ­Pochettino for him to become their head coach if Michael Carrick is sacked. ­Carrick is expected to be fired in line with the recommendation from Jason ­Wilcox, the director of football, and Omar ­Berrada, the chief executive, to Sir Jim Ratcliffe.Pochettino is the USA men’s national team head coach and in August signed a contract to 2030 but he wants the United job after ­managing in the Premier League with Southampton, Tottenham and ­Chelsea.
